target.title: fix: keep native i18n release gates off Blacksmith
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where maintainers using the exact-SHA CI release-gate fallback could remain blocked on Blacksmith capacity because the `native-i18n` job was the only CI job that still selected a Blacksmith runner for manual dispatches.

## Why This Change Was Made

Routes `native-i18n` manual dispatches to the same GitHub-hosted runner used by every other release-gate job. A structural workflow test now rejects any Blacksmith-backed CI job that omits the manual-dispatch fallback, preventing another one-sided routing regression.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Maintainers can use the documented exact-SHA release gate when Blacksmith capacity is unavailable without one native localization job stranding the whole gate.

## Evidence

- Live failure: release gates [28822648843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28822648843) and [28822648526](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28822648526) each completed 108 jobs successfully while only `native-i18n` remained queued on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`.
- `node -e <YAML structural assertion>`: every Blacksmith-backed CI job now routes `workflow_dispatch` to GitHub-hosted capacity.
- `oxfmt --check test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts .github/workflows/ci.yml`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- AWS Crabbox run `run_796b4be95c4c`: `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` passed all 34 tests.
- Exact-head release gate [28824666823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28824666823): all 109 substantive jobs passed; `native-i18n` ran successfully on `ubuntu-24.04` instead of Blacksmith.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: clean, 0.86 confidence.
